description.narrative: CMI!’s vision is a gender-equal and just world where all women, girls, and non-binary, gender non-conforming, trans and intersex people enjoy their rights fully and live to their full potential. Our role in bringing about this vision is to support movements to be resilient and leverage their power to create change from local to global and from global to local, thereby engendering systemic and sustainable change at all levels.

In order for feminist civil society movements to be strong and autonomous39 (an ambitious achievement in itself), self-led WHRDs and WROs go through three intermediate steps - resulting in CMI!’s output (see section 4 and Annex 1, our Results Framework). WHRDs and WROs must be: RESOURCED with the knowledge, resources, and skills for impact, including for L&A. COORDINATED to be able to organise together to articulate priorities and take collective action, including amplifying voices through alliances between structurally excluded movements, linking with more mainstream movements where possible. RESILIENT by having resources, networks, strength and holistic security in place to sustain their work including in the face of backlash and closing civic space, build broader support bases, and expand their work.

Our five-year strategic objective is: political actors, societal actors and donors at local, national, regional and global levels take action to recognise, protect and fulfil the human rights of all women, girls, and non-binary, gender non-conforming, trans and intersex people as a result of strong and autonomous feminist movements holding them to account.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of strengthened alliances and or new alliances created through CMI member interventions, and this includes listing the qualitative indicator of type of alliances.

comment.narrative: The baseline indicator measures new values occurring at the start of the intervention, which has been set at 0.

This reporting measure of this indicator is unique. New or strengthened alliances at different levels will be captured. In case one alliance is created in the first year, we shall only count for that year regardless of the number of times activities will be carried out to strengthen that alliance.

The organisaiton also supported the creation of a new sex worker-led organisation thorugh the collaboration of two mentees. An inspiration for UNESO in collaboration with OGERA to organised and hold the 1st ever National Sex workers’ SRHR Symposium in Uganda which brought together eight one (81) SWs leaders, government officials, parliamentarians, SRHR advocates, health workers, and representatives from civil society organizations, partners, legal representatives and other key populations.

This partnership signifies WAAD's commitment to addressing the intersectional of discrimination faced by women, particularly those affected by HIV/AIDS, by collaborating with NAC, WAAD can leverage their expertise and resources to develop comprehensive programs that support women living with or affected by HIV/AIDS.WAAD actively collaborated with local organizations for example Springs of Life at the ICASA community village exhibition stand, Musasa, WAAD collaborated with Musasa for the 16 Days of Activism campaign, governmental agencies like National AIDS Council (NAC) to leverage resources, share expertise, and coordinate efforts and capacitation as well as CeSHHAR for community clinical services provision. By actively participating in the national and provincial Key and Vulnerable Populations Forum, WAAD played a central role in decision making around the HIV programming response in the sector. Moreover, the forum serves as a platform for WAAD to link and learn with fellow organisations implementing Key and Vulnerable Centred Response. One of WAAD's esteemed partner organizations is the Ministry of Women Affairs, Community, Small and Medium Enterprises Development. This collaboration will allow WAAD to access valuable resources, insights, and support in our endeavour to empower women and promote gender equality. "
